blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Abijah. Three years in Jerusalem, at war with Jeroboam.
REIGNEDi
3 years c. 913–911 BC (dates vary)
CAPITAL
Jerusalem
HOUSE
House of David 2nd of 20 in Judah
VERDICT
✕ Did evil “And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him”
PROPHETS
Iddo the prophet
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS REHOBOAM → ZEDEKIAH
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him”
1 Kings 15:3 (KJV) →
“his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father”
1 Kings 15:3 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO
Kings adds that for David's sake the LORD gave him "a lamp in Jerusalem". 1 Kings 15:4–5
Chronicles gives no verdict. It tells instead of his speech to Israel on Mount Zemaraim and a victory won "because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers". 2 Chronicles 13:4–18
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS
✓ Did right ✕ Did evil ◐ Mixed ● No verdict formula
THE KINGDOM
Jerusalem and the places of the reign
Judah (the south) · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
Kings: he walked in his father's sins. 1 Kings 15:3
Chronicles: in his speech he says Judah kept the priests, the sons of Aaron, the daily offerings, the shewbread and the lamps. 2 Chronicles 13:10–11
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
Id Iddo the prophet Chronicles says Abijah's acts, ways and sayings are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.
TWO ACCOUNTS
Where Kings and Chronicles differ
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.
His name
1 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
His mother
1 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
The verdict and the war
1 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
3 years (1 Kgs 15:2). Scripture gives lengths and cross-dates, never BC years.
THIELE, REVISED BY MCFALL (1991)
Printed form: 913–911/910 (PDF p. 11).
YOUNG (2005), REVISING THIELE
Printed form: 914–912/911 (p. 246 (Table 2)).
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 915–913 (p. 20).
TRADITIONAL DATES (USSHER, 1658)
Printed form: 958–955 (p. 42 (scan leaf n26)).
Two names for one woman
Kimchi and Rashi (as reported in the Pulpit Commentary, 1881); John Gill (1748–63); Jamieson, Fausset and Brown (1871)
She had two names, perhaps taking a new one when she became queen; the names are too unlike for a copying slip. 1 Kings 15:2 2 Chronicles 13:2 [79][108][131]
One woman, granddaughter of Absalom
C. F. Keil (1872); J. R. Lumby (1886); Ellicott's commentary

"Daughter" means granddaughter: Absalom's daughter Tamar married Uriel of Gibeah, and "Michaiah" is a copyist's slip for Maachah, which the Greek, Syriac and Arabic versions read. 2 Samuel 14:27 2 Chronicles 13:2 [24][96][37]
Natural and adoptive fathers
Matthew Poole (1683–85)
She might be the natural daughter of one man and the adopted daughter, or granddaughter, of the other; or Uriel and Absalom were one man. 2 Chronicles 13:2 [120]
Two Maachahs confused
E. Bertheau, after O. Thenius (as reported, and rejected, by C. F. Keil, 1872)
Abijah's mother and Asa's mother were different women whom the text has run together. 1 Kings 15:10 [9]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 6
1 Kings 14 1 Kings 15 2 Chronicles 11 2 Chronicles 12 2 Chronicles 13 2 Chronicles 14
PASSAGES · 6
1 Kings 14:31 1 Kings 15:1–8 2 Chronicles 11:20–22 2 Chronicles 12:16 2 Chronicles 13:1–22 2 Chronicles 14:1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not give Abijah's age when he began to reign.
Kings does not mention the battle of Zemaraim; Chronicles does not repeat Kings' verdict.
Scripture does not say how Abijah died; both books say only that he slept with his fathers.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textKings calls him Abijam and Chronicles Abijah. The two books give the same father, the same cross-date and the same three years, so they are read as one king. 1 Kings 14:31 1 Kings 15:1–2 2 Chronicles 12:16 2 Chronicles 13:1–2
